claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you are enquiring about, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now, could you please tell me: do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you.

Just a couple more questions to confirm your eligibility:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question: Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation provided by the local council?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well... yes, actually. Alex has been in local authority care for a couple of months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. This is important information.

Could you tell me approximately how long Alex has been in local authority care? And during this time, does Alex spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in care for about 12 weeks now. No, he doesn't come home to stay with me - he's at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Since Alex has been in care for more than 8 weeks and doesn't spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you, I need to ask one more question:

Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he is in care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, the local authority is paying for his accommodation and maintenance while he's in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all this information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not currently eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

- **Alex has been in local authority care for 12 weeks**, which exceeds the 8-week limit after which Child Benefit entitlement usually stops for children in care.
- **Alex doesn't spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you**, which could have been an exception allowing eligibility to continue.
- **The local council is paying for Alex's accommodation and maintenance**, which means you cannot receive Child Benefit while this arrangement is in place.

**If your circumstances change in the future**, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. For example, if Alex returns home or begins spending at least 2 nights in a row each week (or 7 or more consecutive days) at home with you, you could potentially make a new claim.

I understand this may not be the news you were hoping for. If you have any questions or your situation changes, I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly for further guidance.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
